Name: Establishing  an LGBTQ+ liaison within the department of veterans’ services.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing an LGBTQ+ liaison within the department of veterans’ services

Attachments.Name: Proposed Int. No. 928-A Fiscal Impact Statement - City Council

Summary: This bill would establish an LGBTQ+ liaison within the department of veterans’ services. The liaison would be tasked with conducting outreach to LGBTQ+ veterans, coordinating the department’s assistance with discharge characterization upgrades for LGBTQ+ veterans, and connecting LGBTQ+ veterans with programs and services offered by the department of veterans’ services and other relevant agencies. The bill would also require the department to issue an annual report related to assistance for LGBTQ+ veterans.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 31-112 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 4 for the year 2022, is amended to read as follows:
§ 31-112 Benefits and assistance for [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veterans. a. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meaning:
Certificate of eligibility. The term "certificate of eligibility" means a certificate issued by the department that can be used as proof that a discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran is eligible for certain city benefits or services available to veterans.
Discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran. The term "discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran" means a veteran who was discharged from the United States military or naval services due solely or in part to (i) sexual orientation, gender identity or expression; (ii) statements, consensual sexual conduct, or consensual acts relating to sexual orientation, gender identity or expression; (iii) the disclosure of such statements, conduct or acts, that were prohibited by the armed forces at the time of discharge; or (iv) for veterans who identify as [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+, untreated trauma, including that resulting from sexual assault which occurred during military service. 
LGBTQ+. The term “LGBTQ+” means lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer/questioning, and other non-heterosexual sexual orientations or non-cisgender gender identities.
   b. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no veteran shall be denied eligibility for any city program, service, or benefit to veterans for which they would otherwise be eligible, solely on the basis of the veteran's status as a discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran.
c. The department shall offer assistance to any discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran seeking a discharge characterization upgrade, change of narrative reasons for discharge, change of separation and separation program designator codes or change of reentry/reenlistment. Such assistance shall be provided by legal counsel or an accredited representative of an organization recognized under section 5902 of title 38 of the United States code or successor provisions.
d. Upon request, the department shall issue a certificate of eligibility to a discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran as proof of their eligibility to receive certain services and benefits for veterans.
e. The department shall:
1. Make available on the department's website information about (i) obtaining certificates of eligibility for discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veterans and (ii) the availability of legal assistance, to any discharged [LGBTQ] LGBTQ+ veteran seeking a discharge characterization upgrade, change of narrative reasons for discharge, change of separation and separation program designator codes or change of reentry/reenlistment; and
2. Conduct outreach through email, social media and other means to raise awareness about such certificates and the availability of such legal assistance.
f. [The department shall periodically review veterans' experience with accessing the assistance required pursuant to subdivision c of this section and shall report any identified issues to the speaker of the council by June 1, 2022, and annually thereafter.] No later than July 31, 2027, and annually by July 31 thereafter, the commissioner shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and shall post on the department’s website a report that shall include: 
1. The number of veterans assisted by the department who identified themselves to the department as LGBTQ+ veterans; 
2. The number of LGBTQ+ veterans known to be eligible for assistance from the department regarding a discharge characterization upgrade pursuant to subdivisions c and d of this section; 
3. The number of LGBTQ+ veterans to whom the department provided assistance regarding a discharge characterization upgrade pursuant to subdivisions c and d of this section;
4. A list of all programs and services to which the department referred veterans who identified themselves to the department as LGBTQ+ veterans; 
5. A description of complaints made by veterans who identified themselves to the department as LGBTQ+ veterans related to such veterans’ experience accessing the assistance required pursuant by this section; 
6. A description of any issues identified by the department related to LGBTQ+ veterans’ ability to access the assistance required pursuant to this section; and 
7. Recommendations for improving access to programs and services for LGBTQ+ veterans.
g. The commissioner shall designate an employee of the department to act as a liaison for LGBTQ+ veterans. The duties of such liaison shall include, but need not be limited to: 
1. Conducting outreach to LGBTQ+ veterans, organizations serving LGBTQ+ veterans, and, where the department determines that it is appropriate and safe to do so, the families of such veterans, to make them aware of the services offered by the department and to provide contact information for the liaison for LGBTQ+ veterans; 
2. Coordinating assistance and outreach provided by the department pursuant to subdivisions c, d, and e of this section; and 
3. Referring LGBTQ+ veterans to relevant programs and services offered by the department and other agencies. 
§ 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
